lessons.title: Hygiene habits in your workplace
lessons.html:
Learning on the job

In this work experience module you work in a real sheep and goat abattoir. A mentor or supervisor guides you and checks your work. You must show that you follow the abattoir's hygiene and sanitising procedures every day. When you do, your mentor signs your logbook.

Every shift you must

  1. Come to work clean, with short, clean nails.
  2. Leave jewellery, watches and phones in your locker.
  3. Change into clean protective clothing in the change room: hairnet first, then overall, apron and white boots.
  4. Wash hands and arms with soap and warm water before you enter the work area.
  5. Go through the boot wash.
  6. Wash hands again after the toilet, breaks, touching your face, and whenever they are dirty or have touched wool.
  7. Cover any cut with a blue waterproof plaster and a glove, and report it.
  8. Report illness before you start.

Do not

  • Eat, drink, smoke, chew gum or spit in work areas.
  • Go outside, to the toilet or the canteen wearing your apron.
  • Move from the dirty area to the clean area without following the plant rules.
  • Put your knife down on the floor or tuck it under your arm.

Wool and dirt from sheep and goats get everywhere. Small hygiene habits, done every time, keep the meat safe.

lessons.title: Sanitising tasks in a small stock abattoir
lessons.html:
Tasks you will help with

  • Picking up wool, skin pieces and fat from floors during the shift.
  • Clearing wool from drain covers.
  • Checking hand-wash basins for soap and paper towels.
  • Checking that knife sterilizers are full and hot.
  • Emptying bins and keeping condemned bins closed.
  • Washing hooks, spreaders, offal trays and containers.
  • Helping with the end-of-shift clean: dry clean, pre-rinse, detergent, scrub, rinse, inspect, sanitise.
  • Cleaning the lairage pens and the off-loading ramp as the schedule says.
  • Washing aprons and boots.

Follow the SOP

Your abattoir has written sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOPs). They say what to clean, with which chemical, at what strength, with which tools and in which order. Ask your mentor to show you the SSOP for each area. Do it the same way every time.

Chemical safety

  • Wear gloves, goggles and an apron when handling chemicals.
  • Measure exactly.
  • Never mix chemicals.
  • Keep chemicals away from meat and packaging.
  • Know where the eye-wash station is.

Machine safety

Never clean a machine that is running. Hoists, skin pullers and conveyors must be switched off and locked out by an authorised person first.

lessons.title: Getting signed off
lessons.html:
How your mentor assesses you

AreaYou are competent when you
Personal hygieneFollow every hygiene rule each day without being reminded
Production cleaningKeep your area clear of wool, fat and waste during the shift
End-of-shift cleanFollow the SSOP steps in order and leave surfaces visibly clean
Chemical useMix correctly and wear PPE
RecordsFill in and sign cleaning checklists honestly

Pre-operational checks

Before slaughter starts each day, the supervisor or quality controller checks that everything is clean. Surfaces may be swabbed to test for germs. If your area fails, it must be cleaned again before slaughter starts. Ask your mentor what was found and learn from it.

Your logbook

  • Write the date, area and tasks each day.
  • Describe what you did in your own words. Example: 'Cleaned the skinning platform: picked up wool, pre-rinsed, applied detergent, scrubbed, rinsed, sanitised.'
  • Attach or list the checklists you signed.
  • Get your mentor's signature soon after the task.
  • Write down incidents, such as a chemical splash, and what was done.
  • Never record work you did not do.

Key points

  • Hygiene rules apply every shift, whether someone is watching or not.
  • Wash hands after touching wool, the toilet, breaks and your face.
  • Follow the abattoir's SSOPs exactly for every area.
  • Never clean a running machine.
  • Keep your logbook honest, up to date and signed by your mentor.
